title: Four proposals for Oxford Student Radio
text: Ben’s proposals ranged from a quarter-hour walk through one part of Oxford to a weekly guide to the Internet and the World-Wide Web. ‘Inspirations’ invited contributors to choose a poem, memory, or practical idea; ‘The Hidden Link’ imagined two regular presenters spinning conspiracy theories.

title: Maxie’s live discussion
text: Two draft invitations on Oxygen 107fm letterhead ask the University Counsellor and Nightline to join a live panel on 14 November. They describe callers’ questions and the option of a pre-recorded contribution. The Nightline letter is signed by Maxie Haddow-Allen.

title: A box of CDs
text: Ben numbered the discs, picked 197 tracks, and supplied the disc and track references, durations, and ranks for the night presenters. The labels name him at St Anne’s; his instructions say the records belonged to him and his brother. Presenters were to tick what they played and check the track against the CD.

title: Five files from one list
text: The BASIC program reads six fields from LIST3.TXT and writes each row into AA, A, B, C, or D. There are eleven AA records, from Jan & Dean’s ‘Dead Man’s Curve’ to Frente!’s ‘Ordinary Angels’ from Vara Radio Holland.

title: The evening’s talking points
text: NightAir notes put Russian and French political news, the Ashes, Pride and Prejudice, and Maradona’s visit to the Oxford Union on the same sheet. Its date is the file’s save date.

title: Writing to Mark Radcliffe
text: In a letter saved in September, Ben said the station had secured a full regional licence starting the following February. He hoped to make a show with live music, poetry, and his charity-shop records. He asked the DJ for an interview and recorded idents.

title: Getting the station built
text: A draft JCR motion in Joe Taylor’s Psion files says the Oxford and Brookes students had secured the city’s frequency and proposes £200 for studio set-up. The same file maps out specialist music and programming roles.

title: Ben’s account of the two licences
text: His college CV records November 1995 to June 1997 as ‘program team leader’ at Oxygen and says he worked on the test licence and full-time broadcasting. A separate application describes his role in originating Dead Air and producing and presenting it weekly.
